# Test Design: Epic 9 - Show the last successful sync time on the technician home screen

**Date:** 2026-09-28
**Author:** tea-eval-harness
**Status:** Draft

---

## Executive Summary

**Scope:** Full test design for Epic 9

**Source note:** This project has no PRD, no architecture document, and no sprint-status file. The epic document `docs/epics/epic-9-last-sync-indicator.md` (Stories 9.1–9.2, Constraints, Acceptance Criteria) is the sole and sufficient requirements source for this run.

**Risk Summary:**

- Total risks identified: 6
- High-priority risks (≥6): 2
- Critical categories: BUS, DATA (the two categories carrying the high-priority risks)

**Coverage Summary:**

- P0 scenarios: 3 (~4–8 hours)
- P1 scenarios: 6 (~8–14 hours)
- P2/P3 scenarios: 3 (~3–6 hours)
- **Total effort**: ~15–28 hours (~2–3.5 days)

---

## Not in Scope

| Item | Reasoning | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Sync engine's own correctness** (writing `lastSuccessfulSyncAt`, publishing the completion event) | The epic states both already exist and are already consumed by the existing progress spinner (Story 9.2); this epic only reads/consumes them, it does not implement them. | Relies on the sync engine's existing coverage, since the same event and field already back shipped functionality (the spinner). |
| **`home_last_sync_row` flag delivery/targeting mechanism** | The epic states this is "an existing feature flag the release process already toggles per organization" (Constraints); this epic adds no flag infrastructure. | Relies on the existing flag system's own operational process and tests. |
| **Localization/i18n of the relative-time phrasing beyond representative boundaries** | The epic states no localization requirement; only representative deltas ("just now", minutes, hours, days) are specified as the display format. | Not tested here; carried as an assumption in Assumptions and Dependencies rather than invented as a risk. |

---

## Risk Assessment

### High-Priority Risks (Score ≥6)

| Risk ID | Category | Description | Probability | Impact | Score | Mitigation | Owner | Timeline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R-001 | BUS | The row re-renders only "when the sync engine publishes a completion event... No polling and no timer is added" (Story 9.2). If the screen stays open without a new sync, the relative-time text silently goes stale, undermining the epic's stated purpose of answering "whether their device is up to date" (Context). | 2 | 3 | 6 | Confirm with product/design whether staleness is accepted behavior; at minimum, cover today's specified behavior with an explicit test so any future change is deliberate. | Feature owner (Dev) to confirm; QA/Test to encode the assertion | Before epic sign-off |
| R-002 | DATA | AC2 requires the row to be omitted when `lastSuccessfulSyncAt` is absent, and Story 9.1 requires "the rest of the screen is unchanged." A bug here would regress an already-working screen for every user, not just those exercising the new feature. | 2 | 3 | 6 | Cover both "field absent" and malformed/unexpected value shapes with tests asserting clean omission and no thrown error. | Dev implementing Story 9.1; QA/Test to verify | Before epic sign-off |

### Medium-Priority Risks (Score 3-4)

| Risk ID | Category | Description | Probability | Impact | Score | Mitigation | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R-003 | TECH | AC3 requires the row to update on sync completion, delivered by subscribing to the event "already publish[ed]... for the existing progress spinner" (Story 9.2). A timing race or miswired subscription could leave the row showing a stale time with no fallback signal. | 2 | 2 | 4 | Add a test that triggers the completion event and asserts the row updates to the new value while the screen is open. | Dev implementing Story 9.2; QA/Test to verify |
| R-004 | BUS | AC4 requires "Turning `home_last_sync_row` off restores the previous home screen exactly." Conditional-rendering changes commonly leave residual spacing/layout artifacts even when the row is hidden. | 2 | 2 | 4 | Add a flag-off test comparing the home screen with the flag on vs. off. | Dev implementing the flag branch; QA/Test to verify |

### Low-Priority Risks (Score 1-2)

| Risk ID | Category | Description | Probability | Impact | Score | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R-005 | PERF | Constraints state "the screen's existing render budget is unchanged." An implementation that re-renders more than the new row on every completion event would silently break this claim. | 1 | 2 | 2 | Document; cover with a lightweight render-count assertion (below), no dedicated performance test justified at this scope. |
| R-006 | SEC | Constraints state the timestamp "exposes nothing to anyone who could not already see it, and it adds no personal data to the screen." A regression would be the value leaking into a channel visible beyond the device holder (logs, analytics) — nothing in the epic adds such a channel today. | 1 | 1 | 1 | Document; no dedicated action beyond the low-cost check below. |

### Risk Category Legend

- **TECH**: Technical/Architecture (flaws, integration, scalability)
- **SEC**: Security (access controls, auth, data exposure)
- **PERF**: Performance (SLA violations, degradation, resource limits)
- **DATA**: Data Integrity (loss, corruption, inconsistency)
- **BUS**: Business Impact (UX harm, logic errors, revenue)
- **OPS**: Operations (deployment, config, monitoring)

**Residual risk:** After the mitigations above, residual exposure is low. R-001 and R-002 close to DOCUMENT/MONITOR-level risk once their coverage rows (below) are green; R-003–R-006 have no further residual action beyond their assigned coverage.

---

## NFR Planning

**Purpose:** Capture epic-specific NFR thresholds, planned validation, and evidence expected for later `nfr-assess`. This is not a final evidence audit.

| NFR Category | Requirement / Threshold | Risk Link | Planned Validation | Evidence Needed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Security | No new data exposure beyond what the device holder already sees; no personal data added. No compliance framework is named in the epic. | R-006 | Component-level test asserting rendering the row triggers no additional network call and no new log/analytics entry | Test report showing zero additional network/log calls |
| Performance | "Existing render budget is unchanged" (qualitative; no numeric figure given). | R-005 | Component-level render-count assertion confirming only the sync row re-renders on the completion event | Render-count assertion output |
| Reliability | Absent/malformed `lastSuccessfulSyncAt` values must not affect the rest of the screen (no numeric threshold beyond "does not break"). | R-002 | Component tests across present/absent/malformed data states | Component test run results (no thrown errors, sibling rows unaffected) |
| Maintainability | Not in scope — no statement in the epic to ground a requirement. | — | N/A | N/A |

**Unknown thresholds:** No maximum acceptable staleness window is defined for the relative-time display (R-001). No numeric render-budget figure is defined (R-005). No compliance framework is named for the security claim (R-006). None of these values are invented here — they remain open clarification items for product/design, not assertable thresholds.

---

## Entry Criteria

- [ ] Requirements and assumptions agreed upon by QA, Dev, PM
- [ ] Test environment/build available with `home_last_sync_row` togglable both on and off
- [ ] Settings-store test fixtures available for both a "synced" state (`lastSuccessfulSyncAt` present) and a "never synced" state (field absent)
- [ ] A way to simulate/dispatch the sync engine's completion event exists in the test environment (reusing whatever the existing progress-spinner tests already use)
- [ ] Feature deployed to test environment

## Exit Criteria

- [ ] All P0 tests passing
- [ ] All P1 tests passing (or failures triaged)
- [ ] No open high-priority / high-severity bugs
- [ ] R-001 (staleness behavior) and R-002 (absent/malformed handling) verified and signed off — both are the score-6 risks gating release
- [ ] Flag-off restoration (R-004 / AC4) confirmed structurally identical to the pre-epic home screen

---

## Test Coverage Plan

### P0 (Critical)

**Criteria**: Critical business, security, data-integrity, or compliance impact with no safe
workaround. Risk score is supporting evidence and is not a required condition.

| Requirement | Test Level | Risk Link | Test Count | Owner | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **9.1-COMP-002** — Home screen renders with no sync row when `lastSuccessfulSyncAt` is absent (AC2) | Component | R-002 | 1 | Dev | Component level because it is a conditional-rendering concern, not pure logic. |
| **9.1-COMP-003** — Home screen does not throw and omits the row for malformed/unexpected stored values (null, empty string, non-parseable) | Component | R-002 | 1 | Dev | Defensive regression guard for a screen that already works for every user today. |
| **9.1-COMP-004** — Every other existing row on the home screen renders unaffected in both present-value and absent-value cases | Component | R-002 | 1 | Dev | Directly verifies "the rest of the screen is unchanged" (Story 9.1). |

**Total P0**: 3 tests, ~4–8 hours

### P1 (High)

**Criteria**: Core, frequent, or complex behavior with material user reach and a limited workaround.
Risk score is supporting evidence and is not a required condition.

| Requirement | Test Level | Risk Link | Test Count | Owner | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **9.1-UNIT-001** — Relative-time formatting function returns correct text for representative deltas and boundaries ("just now", minutes, hours, days) | Unit | - | 1 | Dev | Pure function, no store/UI dependency; underlies every other displayed-text scenario. |
| **9.1-COMP-001** — Home screen renders the sync row with the correctly formatted relative time when `lastSuccessfulSyncAt` is present (AC1) | Component | - | 1 | Dev | Direct AC1 happy path. |
| **9.2-COMP-001** — Row's displayed time updates when the sync engine publishes a completion event while the screen is open (AC3) | Component | R-003 | 1 | Dev | Simulates the existing completion event Story 9.2 says the spinner already consumes. |
| **9.2-COMP-002** — Row's displayed time does not change while the screen is open if no completion event fires | Component | R-001 | 1 | Dev | Encodes today's specified no-timer/no-poll behavior explicitly. |
| **9-E2E-001** — With `home_last_sync_row` off, the home screen matches the pre-epic screen exactly (AC4) | E2E | R-004 | 1 | QA | E2E needed to catch layout-level residue component tests in isolation would miss. |
| **9-E2E-002** — Golden path: sync completes, technician sees the time, a second sync completes while the screen stays open, time updates (AC1 + AC3) | E2E | R-003 | 1 | QA | Full-stack confidence beyond mocked component tests that the settings-store read and real event bus wire together correctly. |

**Total P1**: 6 tests, ~8–14 hours

### P2 (Medium)

**Criteria**: Secondary behavior with narrower user reach and an acceptable workaround. Risk score
is supporting evidence and is not a required condition.

| Requirement | Test Level | Risk Link | Test Count | Owner | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **9.1-COMP-005** — With the flag on and no sync ever completed, the row remains absent (AC2 × AC4 combination) | Component | - | 1 | Dev | Narrower-reach combination check. |

**Total P2**: 1 test, ~1–2 hours

### P3 (Low)

**Criteria**: Rare, cosmetic, or experimental behavior with minimal impact and an easy workaround.
Risk score is supporting evidence and is not a required condition.

| Requirement | Test Level | Risk Link | Test Count | Owner | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **9.2-COMP-003** — Triggering the completion event re-renders only the sync row, not sibling rows/the whole screen | Component | R-005 | 1 | Dev | Render-budget claim; render-count assertion is sufficient, no k6/load tooling justified at this scope. |
| **9.1-COMP-006** — Rendering the row triggers no additional network call and no new log/analytics entry | Component | R-006 | 1 | Dev | Verifies the "no personal data / no network call" claim. |

**Total P3**: 2 tests, ~2–4 hours

---

## Execution Strategy

**Philosophy:** Run every functional scenario in pull requests while the suite stays under 15 minutes.
Defer only work with material infrastructure or duration cost. P0 through P3 are priority and are not
execution timing; this section decides when tests run and the coverage plan above decides what they are.

- **Pull request:** All Unit and Component scenarios (`9.1-UNIT-001`, `9.1-COMP-001` through `9.1-COMP-006`, `9.2-COMP-001` through `9.2-COMP-003`) — no device/app-boot overhead, fast feedback, target duration well under 15 minutes.
- **Nightly:** The two E2E/device-flow scenarios (`9-E2E-001`, `9-E2E-002`) if device/app-boot time makes them too slow for the PR budget; re-evaluate for PR inclusion once actual E2E runtime is known.
- **Weekly:** None identified for this epic — no load, chaos, or large-dataset work applies to a local, no-network, no-storage read.

Do not re-list the individual tests here. They are already in the coverage plan.

---

## Resource Estimates

### Test Development Effort

| Priority | Count | Total Hours | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | 3 | ~4–8 hours | Regression-guard component tests for absent/malformed data |
| P1 | 6 | ~8–14 hours | Core AC coverage plus the two E2E scenarios |
| P2 | 1 | ~1–2 hours | Single combination check |
| P3 | 2 | ~2–4 hours | Low-cost render-budget and no-network-call checks |
| **Total** | **12** | **~15–28 hours** | **~2–3.5 days** |

### Prerequisites

**Test Data:**

- Settings-store fixture representing a device that completed a sync (`lastSuccessfulSyncAt` present with a representative timestamp)
- Settings-store fixture representing a never-synced device (field absent)
- A malformed-value fixture (null / empty string / non-parseable) for the defensive regression guard (9.1-COMP-003)

**Tooling:**

- The project's UI/component test runner — not yet confirmed in this repository; no source tree, `package.json`, or test tooling exists in `field-sync-indicator/` as of this run
- A way to simulate/dispatch the sync engine's completion event within tests, reusing whatever the existing progress-spinner tests already use (Story 9.2)

**Environment:**

- Test build with `home_last_sync_row` togglable both on and off
- Device/app build with the existing sync engine wired in

---

## Quality Gate Criteria

### Pass/Fail Thresholds

- **P0 pass rate**: 100% (no exceptions) — protects the already-working home screen from regression
- **P1 pass rate**: ≥95% (waivers required for failures)
- **P2/P3 pass rate**: ≥90% (informational)
- **High-risk mitigations**: 100% complete (R-001, R-002) or approved waivers

### Coverage Targets

Given the small, fully enumerable scope of this epic (4 acceptance criteria, 6 grounded risks), the target is **100% of the 12 listed scenarios**, not a percentage proxy across generic categories that don't map cleanly onto a single-screen, no-backend, no-network feature.

### Non-Negotiable Requirements

- [ ] All P0 tests pass
- [ ] No high-risk (≥6) items unmitigated (R-001, R-002)
- [ ] Security scenario (R-006, 9.1-COMP-006) passes 100%
- [ ] Performance regression check (R-005, 9.2-COMP-003) passes — no numeric SLA exists for this local-only read
- [ ] Planned NFR evidence exists or `nfr-assess` has documented CONCERNS/waivers

---

## Mitigation Plans

### R-001: Staleness of the relative-time display without a new sync event (Score: 6)

**Mitigation Strategy:**

1. Confirm with product/design whether the current no-timer/no-poll behavior is accepted or needs a lightweight local refresh mechanism.
2. Regardless of that decision, cover today's specified behavior with `9.2-COMP-002` so any future change is a deliberate, tested decision rather than a silent regression.

**Owner:** Feature owner (Dev) to confirm behavior; QA/Test to encode the assertion
**Timeline:** Before epic sign-off
**Status:** Planned
**Verification:** `9.2-COMP-002` passes and the product/design decision is recorded (accepted-as-is, or a follow-up story is opened)

### R-002: Absent/malformed sync-timestamp handling regresses the home screen (Score: 6)

**Mitigation Strategy:**

1. Implement and pass `9.1-COMP-002` (clean omission when absent).
2. Implement and pass `9.1-COMP-003` (no throw on malformed values).
3. Implement and pass `9.1-COMP-004` (sibling rows unaffected in both states).

**Owner:** Dev implementing Story 9.1; QA/Test to verify
**Timeline:** Before epic sign-off
**Status:** Planned
**Verification:** All three linked test IDs pass in CI before merge

---

## Assumptions and Dependencies

### Assumptions

1. The sync engine already reliably writes `lastSuccessfulSyncAt` on every successful sync and already publishes a completion event consumed by the existing progress spinner (Epic Context, Story 9.2) — this epic only consumes both, it does not implement them.
2. `home_last_sync_row` already exists as a working, per-organization-toggleable flag in the release process (Constraints) — this epic builds no flag infrastructure.
3. No PRD, architecture document, or sprint-status file exists for this project; the epic document is the complete and sufficient requirements source for this run.

### Dependencies

1. Test environment/build with the existing sync engine and `home_last_sync_row` flag available, toggleable both on and off — required before test execution begins.
2. A way to simulate or drive the sync engine to (a) complete a sync producing a `lastSuccessfulSyncAt` value and (b) leave the field absent — required before `9.1-COMP-001`/`9.1-COMP-002` and `9-E2E-002` can run.

### Risks to Plan

- **Risk**: The staleness threshold behind R-001 is undefined by product/design.
  - **Impact**: `9.2-COMP-002` can only assert today's specified behavior (no change without an event); it cannot validate against a real staleness limit because none exists.
  - **Contingency**: Escalate to product/design for a decision before treating R-001 as fully closed; document the open clarification regardless of test pass/fail.

---

## Follow-on Workflows (Manual)

- Run `/bmad-testarch-atdd` to generate failing P0 tests (separate workflow; not auto-run).
- Run `/bmad-testarch-automate` for broader coverage once implementation exists.

## Assumptions and Dependencies

### Assumptions

1. The sync engine already reliably writes `lastSuccessfulSyncAt` on every successful sync and already publishes a completion event consumed by the existing progress spinner (Epic Context, Story 9.2) — this epic only consumes both, it does not implement them.
2. `home_last_sync_row` already exists as a working, per-organization-toggleable flag in the release process (Constraints) — this epic builds no flag infrastructure.
3. No PRD, architecture document, or sprint-status file exists for this project; the epic document is the complete and sufficient requirements source for this run.

### Dependencies

1. Test environment/build with the existing sync engine and `home_last_sync_row` flag available, toggleable both on and off — required before test execution begins.
2. A way to simulate or drive the sync engine to (a) complete a sync producing a `lastSuccessfulSyncAt` value and (b) leave the field absent — required before `9.1-COMP-001`/`9.1-COMP-002` and `9-E2E-002` can run.

### Risks to Plan

- **Risk**: The staleness threshold behind R-001 is undefined by product/design.
  - **Impact**: `9.2-COMP-002` can only assert today's specified behavior (no change without an event); it cannot validate against a real staleness limit because none exists.
  - **Contingency**: Escalate to product/design for a decision before treating R-001 as fully closed; document the open clarification regardless of test pass/fail.

scoredRiskDescriptions: The row re-renders only "when the sync engine publishes a completion event... No polling and no timer is added" (Story 9.2). If the screen stays open without a new sync, the relative-time text silently goes stale, undermining the epic's stated purpose of answering "whether their device is up to date" (Context).

AC2 requires the row to be omitted when lastSuccessfulSyncAt is absent, and Story 9.1 requires "the rest of the screen is unchanged." A bug here would regress an already-working screen for every user, not just those exercising the new feature.

AC3 requires the row to update on sync completion, delivered by subscribing to the event "already publish[ed]... for the existing progress spinner" (Story 9.2). A timing race or miswired subscription could leave the row showing a stale time with no fallback signal.
AC4 requires "Turning home_last_sync_row off restores the previous home screen exactly." Conditional-rendering changes commonly leave residual spacing/layout artifacts even when the row is hidden.
